skill.name: when-validating-code-works-use-functionality-audit
skill.description: Guides an AI coding assistant through evidence-based functionality validation using sandbox setup, realistic test execution, debugging, regression checks, and readiness reporting.
skill.summary: Validate generated or modified code by running real tests, debugging failures, and reporting production readiness.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it is execution-heavy and includes many real shell, package installation, Docker, temporary-directory, and filesystem operations. Several static hits are false positives caused by markdown backticks, local test examples, dummy environment values, and in-process supertest calls. Manual review is recommended before running the workflow automatically.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are presented as runnable workflow steps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx, npm install, Docker, rm, or command-substitution examples, and show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: Sandbox examples use predictable paths under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp-created directories with restrictive permissions and avoid deleting fixed shared paths.

remediation.issue: The workflow writes generated tests, logs, reports, and environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all generated artifacts inside the approved sandbox and avoid copying real secrets into test .env files.

content.user_title: Validate Code Functionality With Real Tests
content.value_statement: Generated code can look complete while still failing at runtime. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through sandbox setup, realistic execution, debugging, and readiness checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates a structured sandbox workflow for testing generated or modified code.
Runs unit, integration, edge case, and regression tests with captured logs.
Uses test output and coverage data to classify failures by root cause.
Guides iterative fixes while checking for regressions after each change.
Produces a readiness report with test counts, coverage, and deployment status.
limitations: Requires local tools such as npm, pytest, Docker, or claude-flow when the workflow uses them.
The examples focus mainly on JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and API testing patterns.
It cannot prove production safety without representative data, dependencies, and environment variables.
Shell commands and sandbox paths should be reviewed before running in sensitive repositories.

use_cases.title: Verify generated features
use_cases.description: Run a structured audit after an AI assistant writes code, so passing behavior is demonstrated with tests instead of assumed.

use_cases.title: Debug failing implementations
use_cases.description: Use captured logs, root cause grouping, and retesting steps to turn failing generated code into working code.

use_cases.title: Prepare release evidence
use_cases.description: Create a concise readiness report that summarizes tests run, coverage, regressions, and remaining blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Basic functionality check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate the recent code change. Set up the smallest safe sandbox, run the relevant tests, and tell me whether the code really works.

prompt_templates.title: Debug test failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for failing generated code
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a functionality audit on this module. Capture failing tests, classify the root causes, apply minimal fixes, and rerun the same tests to verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Regression-focused audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this branch for functional regressions. Run existing tests, add realistic edge-case tests where coverage is weak, and report any behavior that changed unexpectedly.

prompt_templates.title: Production readiness review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the full functionality audit process for this service. Include sandbox setup, integration tests, coverage review, regression checks, and a final readiness recommendation.

output_examples.input: Validate the new authentication helper before I merge it.
output_examples.output: The audit ran targeted unit tests and one integration path. The happy path passed, invalid credentials failed correctly, and one token-expiry edge case still needs a fix.

output_examples.input: Check whether the generated API endpoint actually works.
output: Sandbox created with test dependencies installed.
Endpoint tests covered success, authentication failure, and malformed input.
The endpoint returned the expected status codes, but coverage missed database error handling.

output_examples.input: Rerun validation after the bug fix.
output_examples.output: The original failing test now passes, the regression suite stayed green, and coverage remained above the configured threshold. The code is ready for review.

best_practices: Run commands in an isolated disposable workspace before using the workflow on important files.
Start with the smallest meaningful test set, then expand to integration and regression tests.
Keep the final report tied to observed evidence: commands run, test results, coverage, and remaining failures.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated test files as proof unless the tests execute and assert real behavior.
Do not run dependency installation or Docker commands without reviewing their effect on the local environment.
Do not mark code production-ready when environment variables, external services, or critical integrations were mocked away.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It validates whether code runs correctly by creating a test environment, executing tests, debugging failures, and reporting readiness.

faq.question: Does it write or modify code?
faq.answer: The workflow can generate tests and guide fixes. Review proposed changes before applying them to important branches.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: It uses shell commands, package installation, temporary directories, and optional Docker commands. Manual review is recommended before execution.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits projects with executable tests or clear runtime behavior, especially JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and API services.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the code or branch to validate, expected behavior, test commands, environment requirements, and any known failing cases.
